answer: Proposed mesa audit: each paid key commits a distinct cipher-masked 80-GiB file before a surprise 90-second upload window. Independent receivers hash each full stream and timestamp it; validators accept only timely matching receipts. A farm can share a model and rent a bulk link, but each clone needs another live 10-Gbps uplink lane at once; different masks defeat multicast. Leased lanes still cost per concurrent slot and cannot be reused in that window. If bytes are missing, that key falls to nadir and forfeits pending pay. Receivers and validators must enforce this; MinePoA does not.
